title: Google’s AI Mode now lets you attach up to 10 photos at once
summary: You can finally attach multiple photos in AI Mode without opening the camera every time.
content: TL;DR Google is rolling out support for capturing multiple photos at once with the AI Mode camera. It replaces the shutter button with a plus icon and lets users attach up to 10 images at once. The change is rolling out with the latest version of the Google app. Google has been steadily adding input options to AI Mode in the Google app. We’ve seen Google working to add PDF uploads to AI Mode and even a share sheet shortcut for attaching files . Now, we’ve spotted the company rolling out yet another small but useful change to the AI Mode camera. In the latest version of the Google app (v17.78.13), the camera in AI Mode’s compose box is getting an upgrade. Until now, the Lens icon in AI Mode opened a camera interface that let you capture and attach an image for AI Mode queries. If you wanted to add another, you had to open the camera interface again. That’s now changing. The camera interface now has a plus button in place of the usual shutter button. You can tap it once to capture an image, then tap it again to capture another.

title: I’ve used the Pixel 11 Pro XL for months, and I wouldn’t go without these 6 accessories

content: I’ve been using the Google Pixel 11 Pro XL since it launched globally in August, and after a few months, I’ve started paying closer attention to how well it holds up over time. Buying an expensive smartphone is one thing, but keeping it in good condition months or even years later takes a little more effort. No matter how careful I am, daily use eventually takes a toll, whether it’s a scratch, an accidental drop, or the battery slowly losing its ability to hold a charge. I’ve realized that something as simple as using a good case, protecting the screen, and being mindful of how I charge my phone can go a long way in keeping it in good shape. Over the past few months, I’ve also figured out which accessories are actually worth spending money on. So, if you’ve recently bought a Pixel 11 Pro XL, here are six accessories I’d recommend investing in to keep your phone looking and working at its best for as long as possible.

title: The tiny $449 enough phone just got a huge battery, storage, and RAM upgrade
summary: Crowdfunders will get 50% more RAM, double the storage, and a beefier silicon-carbon battery.
content: TL;DR The enough phone is trying to offer a throwback Android experience with its 5.3-inch display and compact, pocket-friendly build. When first announced earlier this month, the phone was set to get 8GB of RAM, 128GB storage, and a 3,500mAh battery. Instead of that, it will now ship with 12GB of RAM, 256GB storage, and a 3,850mAh silicon-carbon battery. In 2026, we’ve all started getting used to the idea of phones trying to do more with less , as RAM and chip shortages impact production everywhere, but one upstart is now bucking that trend, as the tiny enough phone scores a surprise spec upgrade. We first heard of the enough phone earlier this month. The crowdfunded handset was envisioned as a response to design trends that have pushed smartphones into larger and larger territory, prompting its creators to instead go with a 5.3-inch screen that’s much smaller than what you’ll find on the vast majority of handsets out there.

title: Samsung Galaxy Z TriFold 2 codename leak hints at another limited release
summary: Internal naming pattern offers clues about Samsung's plans.
content: TL;DR Samsung is reportedly developing the Galaxy Z TriFold 2 under the codename Q9m. Samsung’s previous foldables with similar codename patterns never received global releases, suggesting the TriFold 2 could follow suit. Earlier reports pointed to increased TriFold production in 2027, but higher production volumes wouldn’t necessarily guarantee wider availability. Samsung’s first Galaxy Z TriFold was a $2,899 smartphone that many people couldn’t buy even if they could afford it. The phone was sold in limited quantities across a handful of markets before Samsung pulled the plug just months after launch. Those hoping its successor, the Galaxy TriFold 2 , would be easier to get their hands on may be in for another disappointment, according to a fresh leak. According to Dutch publication GalaxyClub , Samsung is developing its second-generation TriFold under the codename Q9m. The upcoming Galaxy Z Fold 9 and Fold 9 Ultra carry the H9 and Q9 codenames, respectively. Rather than assigning the TriFold 2 a distinct codename, Samsung appears to be treating it as a variation of the Fold 9 Ultra, at least internally.

title: Gemini for Home gets faster responses, smoother chats, and fixes for follow-up and music bugs
summary: Everyday voice commands should feel a little less frustrating.
content: TL;DR Google has fully rolled out speed improvements for common Gemini for Home smart home commands. The latest update fixes bugs affecting follow-up commands and stopping media playback. Google is also rolling out an improved Gemini Live experience, more expressive storytelling, and web answer sources on supported smart displays. The story of Gemini for Home’s transition from Google Assistant is beginning to take a more positive turn. We’ve seen some users warming up to Google’s new voice assistant , particularly after noticeable improvements in response times. Now, Google is giving Gemini more polish, whether you’re asking it to switch off the lights or tell your kids a bedtime story. With its second November update , Google has confirmed that speed improvements for common smart home commands have fully rolled out to Gemini for Home Early Access users. So, whether you’re turning on the lights or adjusting the thermostat, Gemini should respond and act faster.

title: Google Home is sorting out issues with speakers, cameras, lights, and more
summary: Your smart home sounds like it's about to get a little bit smarter.
content: TL;DR Google Home is getting some new features and fixes for speakers, cameras, lights, and thermostats. Home Premium users will no longer have to configure all their cameras separately. Google’s smoothing out issues with transferring music playback to a new speaker or display. Big changes are on the way for your Google-powered smart home, with Assistant finally scheduled to go away for good next summer — that’s still months off, though, and in the meantime we’ve got a fresh batch of Google Home updates to check out. Today Google’s sharing its latest set of new features and bugfixes coming to Home , and it looks like there are quite a few in here that are worth paying attention to. For starters, owners of those affordable Walmart Onn smart cameras can now use Familiar Faces with outdoor models. Other camera upgrades include support for clip feedback when multiple users are configured as admins, as well as manual controls for camera security sirens. We’re also getting bugfixes for event notification previews, event-based video history, and camera controls in landscape view.

title: One UI 9.5 may try to sell you Samsung Care Plus if you drop your Galaxy phone
summary: One UI 9.5 Beta 1 code shows Warranty Care uses drop sensor data to trigger protection plan ads without mentioning the fall.
content: Credit: Shimul Sood / Android Authority TL;DR Code in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 shows Samsung’s Warranty Care app (v1.9.50.23) uses phone drop data to trigger Samsung Care Plus sales notifications. A single drop of 90cm or more onto a hard surface, or three drops of 60cm or more within 30 days, can trigger a default-on “Marketing” notification that doesn’t mention the fall. Drop logs remain stored locally on the device for 30 days. Signing up for Samsung Care Plus after a drop will usually not cover damage that has already occurred. If you drop your Galaxy phone after updating to One UI 9.5, Samsung might follow up with a sales pitch for Samsung Care Plus. Code in the One UI 9.5 Beta 1 build for the Galaxy S26 Ultra shows that Samsung’s Warranty Care app will be able to use your Galaxy phone’s drop detection, including how far it fell and what it landed on, to decide when to recommend Samsung Care Plus. The notifications won’t mention the drop, though, and they arrive in a “Marketing” notification category that’s switched on by default. Warranty Care is the app behind the “Warranty and care hub” in Settings. We first spotted the app hidden in an early One UI 9 build in March, and the Warranty hub debuted with One UI 9 on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 series before reaching the Galaxy S26 series. It puts your warranty status, diagnostics, repair bookings, and Samsung Care Plus sign-ups in one place, so you don’t have to dig through separate apps and websites when something goes wrong.

title: Galaxy Watch is reportedly no longer summing up multi-activity sessions, and users are upset
summary: But an easy fix to the problem is to create a workout routine.
content: Credit: Brady Snyder / Android Authority TL;DR Samsung appears to have changed how it displays stats for multiple activities in a single session. Previously, it would stack details and show them collectively after a workout. But now, it is reportedly only showing stats from the last activity. A workout at a gym may involve more than one activity, which is why smartwatches such as the Galaxy Watch let you record a series of workouts or create custom routines. At the end of the workout, it shows the entire duration of your workout along with the calories burned. However, Samsung may have recently changed how the Galaxy Watch displays these stats, leaving regular users upset. Instead of showing the duration and calories for the entire workout, the Galaxy Watch now shows them only for the last leg of the workout. A report about this change emerges from the Samsung Community in Korea , where the poster shares images comparing how the same activities are displayed differently.

title: Samsung quietly expands Modes and Routines with AI and 7 presets in One UI 9.5
summary: You can ask Gemini or Perplexity, but only Perplexity answers automatically.
content: Credit: Adamya Sharma / Android Authority TL;DR One UI 9.5 Beta 1 adds an “Ask AI assistant” action to Samsung’s Modes and Routines app that can send prompts to Gemini or Perplexity. In our testing, Perplexity automatically sends prompts and reads answers aloud hands-free, whereas Gemini only prefills the prompt and waits for a manual tap because the Google app blocks Samsung’s auto-send request. The update also unlocks text summarization, offline translation, image text extraction, and a Repeat loop action. There are also seven new preset routines, including a Morning news briefing that only works hands-free when switched to Perplexity. Samsung’s Modes and Routines has quietly become one of the most useful parts of One UI for power users. It lets you automate almost anything on your Galaxy phone with simple “if this, then that” rules. With the One UI 9.5 beta, Routines can now hand tasks to an AI assistant as well. Samsung didn’t mention this in the One UI 9.5 beta changelog , but we tried it on our Galaxy S26 Ultra, and which AI assistant you pick makes a big difference. APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship. Routines can now ask Gemini or Perplexity for you Modes and Routines v5.2.00.69 in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 adds a new action called “Ask AI assistant.” You pick an assistant, type a prompt into the “Enter command” box, and the routine sends it whenever its trigger fires, whether that’s dismissing your alarm, arriving at work, or tapping a button. The prompt can also include text from earlier actions in the routine, going up to 8,000 characters.

title: WhatsApp catches up to Google Messages with scheduling for texts, photos, and videos
summary: Messages can be set 10 minutes to 14 days ahead of time.
content: TL;DR WhatsApp now lets you schedule messages 10 minutes to 14 days ahead of time in individual and group chats. The feature works with texts, photos, and video in both one-on-one and group chats. Competitors Google Messages, Signal, and Telegram have had scheduled messages for a while. Lots of things can keep you from being a reliable texter, including thinking of the right thing to say but at the wrong time, and WhatsApp is now able to help out with that by adding support for scheduled messages. Today, the messaging app announced that it’s adding the ability for users to schedule messages to send at a future point. WhatsApp says this has been one of the features that users requested most. Scheduled messaging was already available on Google Messages , Signal, and Telegram, so it finally brings WhatsApp up to speed with the competition.

title: WhatsApp preps travel eSIM discovery, installation, and management tools (Update: Official)
summary: WhatsApp could soon be your one-stop shop for all things eSIM.
content: TL;DR WhatsApp appears to be developing a system for eSIM discovery, purchase, installation, and management. Users would be able to search for eSIMs based on specific travel destinations. Automated tools could wait to activate the eSIM until you arrive where you’re headed. Update, November 26, 2026 (2:11 PM ET): WhatsApp has just confirmed its travel eSIM feature.
